label: rejected

evidence.V1: Reads as a daisy-type flower from front, three-quarter, top (6-petal bloom with gold centre) and silhouette.
evidence.V2: Clear hierarchy: big bloom, medium leaves and stem, small gold centre; petals add a secondary rhythm.
evidence.V3: Stem is a perfectly straight uniform cylinder and the bloom sits flat on top; leaves have a nice curve but overall stiff.
evidence.V4: Petals are chamfered/faceted solids while leaves are paper-thin cards with knife edges and the stem has no edge interest; inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Bloom close-up (studio and flat) shows jagged saw-tooth intersection lines where overlapping petals cut into each other; centre penetrates petals 0.058.
evidence.V6: Red petals, gold centre (kit accent), leaf green in 2 values - disciplined; colourways bluebell/sunset keep it.
evidence.V7: 560 tris vs small target 600 - under target.
evidence.V8: Vertex-colour material and leaf-green secondary match spec, but petals are faceted separate shells rather than fused smooth organic forms.
evidence.V9: Foliage flags correct (Anchored, no collision/touch/query, Box, Color white, bottom-centre origin).

evidence.V1: Clear flower silhouette (bloom, stem, two leaves) from front, three-quarter, top and silhouette.
evidence.V2: Bloom as the big read, stem and leaves medium, gold centre small - clear hierarchy.
evidence.V3: Bloom proportions are good but the stem is a perfectly straight uniform cylinder and the leaves are flat cards, so the plant reads stiff.
evidence.V4: Petals have hard faceted creases while the leaves are paper-thin razor edges; no consistent rounded edge treatment.
evidence.V5: bloom_flat shows petals interpenetrating with jagged zig-zag intersections and faceted petal planes; leaves pierce the stem.
evidence.V6: Petal hue in 2-3 values, leaf green secondary, gold centre accent - disciplined across colourways.
evidence.V8: One white vertex-colour material and kit hues match, but the faceted petals and razor leaf cards do not match the smooth fused shells of the nature kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, CanCollide/CanTouch/CanQuery off, Box fidelity, Color white, SmoothPlastic - correct foliage flags.

evidence.V1: Reads as a flower from front, three-quarter, top (six-petal rosette with gold centre) and silhouette.
evidence.V2: Clear tiers: bloom head (big), stem and two leaves (medium), domed gold centre (small).
evidence.V3: Bloom size is pleasingly exaggerated, but the stem is a perfectly straight uniform tube and the leaves are flat cards; partly stylised.
evidence.V4: Petals have hard faceted bevels while leaves are razor-thin cards with sharp tips; edge treatment is inconsistent across parts.
evidence.V5: Bloom close-ups (studio and flat) show jagged, stepped edges where petals interpenetrate (right side of the head) and stray hard facets across petal tops; minor.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: one petal hue in 2-3 values, leaf-green secondary, gold centre; bluebell and sunset colourways keep the structure.
evidence.V7: 560 tris vs small target 600, under target.
evidence.V8: One vertex-colour material and kit palette, but organic parts are separate shells (petals overlapping, leaves stuck on the stem base) rather than the kit's fused smooth shells.
evidence.V9: Foliage studio line correct (anchored, CanCollide/CanTouch/CanQuery off, white colour, origin bottom-centre); seats pass with no gaps.

artifacts: Saw-tooth intersection seams between overlapping petals
Thin card leaves with knife-edge tips at stem junction
Jagged petal-petal intersections in bloom close-up
Leaf cards razor-thin, left leaf pierces the stem
jagged stepped edges where petals overlap/interpenetrate (bloom close-up, right side)
stray hard facets across petal surfaces
leaves are paper-thin cards with the left leaf tucked behind the stem base
top_fixes: Re-space or fuse petals so they no longer interpenetrate with jagged seams
Give the stem a slight S-curve and taper, and tilt the bloom
Thicken leaves slightly with a soft rim to match the chamfered petals
Rebuild petals as smooth cupped shells that overlap cleanly (or fuse into one bloom shell) to remove jagged intersections
Give the stem a slight curve/taper and the leaves some thickness and a midrib fold
Add a small leaf base or sepal ring under the bloom to tie head to stem
Smooth/fuse the petal ring so overlaps do not create zig-zag edges and petals shade softly
Give the stem a gentle curve and taper and thicken/curl the leaves so they read as fused organic forms
Add a slight root flare or small ground tuft at the stem base so it seats naturally
